caption: The drawing depicts a pair of wooden saloon-style doors, each door appearing nearly symmetrical to the other and composed of a dark reddish-brown wood with visible grain patterns. The top portion of each door features four turned wooden spindles arranged vertically and set within a rectangular frame. Below the spindles, each door has three vertical wooden panels, bordered by horizontal and vertical supports, and secured at the corners and mid-sections with small round metal fasteners. Near the meeting edge of the two doors, there is a round doorknob and keyhole on the right door. The background is plain and off-white, with no additional objects or patterns, and the artist's name and the year 1938 are written in small script in the lower right corner.
title: Doors to Baptistry - Mission San Juan Bautista
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
